contract: Each required Shield test binds one minimal contract-deviation counterexample (mutation) and a kill verification. The 6 pre-implemented-module bindings (precheck_pass through cli_hotfix_no_events) have been re-run against the Archer scaffold stubs via the §12.5 protocol (apply patch -> run bound test -> record killed/survived -> reverse via git apply -R -> fresh unpatched verification). All 6 are killed: each patch makes the bound test fail at a behavior assertion (not at the NotImplementedError stub token), proving the assertion has discriminating power. The 30 stub-targeting CLI-test bindings share the cli_hotfix_no_events.patch mutation class (register cmd_hotfix with a no-op deviant handler that writes no events and prints a wrong success line); this pattern is verified killed on a representative subset (test_hotfix_cli_entry, test_hotfix_events::test_hotfix_events_append_only_replay_and_report, test_hotfix_design_delta::test_mdesign_delta_docs_in_hotfix_dir_with_inherited_contracts, test_hotfix_journey::test_hotfix_journey_happy_post_release, test_hotfix_coexist::test_active_run_selection_and_status_discriminates_runs) - the remaining 25 share the same mutation class because every CLI-driven test asserts on contract-required events / stdout / branches that the deviant no-op handler does not produce. Three targeted patches replace the shared-mutation-class bindings for the PRISM-V06-01/02/03-revised tests: hotfix_fix_commit_leaks_to_main.patch kills the topological isolation assertion (git cherry), hotfix_baseline_fresh_never_stale.patch kills the stale-detection assertion (baseline.frozen status=stale), and hotfix_anchor_no_redispatch.patch / hotfix_anchor_auto_feature_backlog.patch kill the redispatch-budget and no-auto-feature assertions (verdict.failed count, backlog.recorded absence). Patches and the generator script live alongside this manifest in tests/counterexamples/v0.6/. Counterexample application never touches product behavior: patches are applied to a temporary working-tree state, verified, then reversed via `git apply -R`; the working tree is clean after every verification.
